Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwww.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 121 s. 2022 October 10, 2022 Atty. MELCHOR JAEMOND A. ARANAS Atty. PAOLO A. PUNSALAN Atty. ANNA OLIVIA S. LEE Belgica Aranas Baldueza Dela Cruz and Associates Suite 107 AIC Burgundy Empire Tower, ADB Avenue corner Garnet Road, Ortigas, Pasig City Dear Attys. Aranas, Punzalan and Lee: This has reference to your earlier letter requesting for legal opinion from this Department on how will the appointment of the barangay secretary be recognized as valid in accordance with law even without the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang barangay members. Per your letter, Punong Barangay of San Antonio, San Pedro, Laguna, Eugenio S. Ynion, Jr., has appointed Ms. Geslani "Pepped' Jimenez as Barangay Secretary of Barangay San Antonio for the years October 2016 to January 2018 and April 16, 2020 pursuant to Section 3941 of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991. You represented that members of Sanggunian Barangay of San Antonio did not concur to the appointment of Ms. Jimenez as Barangay Secretary nor did they issue a resolution of non-concurrence thereto. But nonetheless, they assailed the validity Of her appointment. Also, you represented that Ms. Jimenez has been performing the functions Of Barangay Secretary and the same has been duly recognized by the Barangay. Hence, the herein request for clarification. May it be respectfully informed that the issue raised herein has already been discussed and settled in DILG Legal Opinion No. 17, S. 20092, pertinent portion of which reads: I SECTION 394. Barangay Secretary: Appointment, Qualifications, Powers and Duties. — (a) The barangay secretary shall be appointed by the punong barangay with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang barangay members. The appointment of the barangay secretary shall not be subject to attestation by the Civil Service Commission. 2 March 25, 2009 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

"Article II, Sections 4 and 5 of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2002-150 provide that: Section 4. Pending Compliance with the condition of concurrence, the appointee, in the exigency of public service, shall be allowed to discharge and perform the powers, duties and responsibilities pertaining to the office and they shall be considered to be holding a temporary appointment. Section 5. Pursuant to Section 5 of RA 6713, otherwise known as the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Official and Employees" the Sanggunian Barangay shall act on the appointment within fifteen (15) working days from receipt of the appointment as submitted by the punong barangay." In the case of Alquizola V. Oc013, the Supreme Court ruled that "the power to appoint is to be exercised conjointly by the Punong Barangay and a majority of all the members of the sangguniang barangay." Such beinq the case. the correlative duty of the members of the Sanqqquniang Barangay being referred to would now be the required concurrence. and pending concurrence, beinq the final phase of the appointment. shall make the appointment temporary. " Applying the above-cited provisions of the Section 394 of the LGC, DILG Memorandum and the Supreme Court ruling in the matter at hand, the appointment of the barangay secretary may only be recognized as valid in accordance with law upon the concurrence by the majority members of the Sanggunian Barangay. Without the conjoint action of appointment and concurrence, neither an appointment nor a replacement can be effectual.4 Nonetheless, the appointed Secretary may assume her duties in an acting capacity pending concurrence by the majority members of the Sangguniang Barangay. However, once the Sangguniang Barangay expresses officially its non-concurrence to the appointment, the barangay secretary shall not anymore be allowed to perform her duties.5 May it be emphasized, however, that while the power to concur is given to the Sangguniang Barangay, said body is not vested with so much plenary discretionary powers. The power to concur is intended for the sanggunian to determine whether or not the appointee of the Punong Barangay possesses all the qualifications prescribed for Barangay Secretary under the LGC and such other qualifications provided by existing laws. If the appointee, therefore, possesses all the qualifications provided by law, then the Sangguniang Barangay has no other far-reaching powers except to issue the concurrence.6 Consequently, the appointee shall be allowed to discharge and perform the powers, duties and responsibilities pertaining to the office and shall be considered to beholding a temporary appointment in the exigency of public service, pending compliance with the condition of concurrence. As such, Ms. Jimenez is entitled to receive her honoraria 3 G.R. NO. 123413, August 27, 1999 4 Ibid s Supra at 2 6 Ibid "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

and other allowances/remuneration from the first day she assumed to the office of the Barangay Secretary.7 Be that as it may, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY RITY OF THE SECRETARY: ANV TOR R.
